behavior: Given the fixture tree's single-module project (its own standalone pom.xml with no <modules>) and its multi-module reactor as two separate roots, resolving any path under the single-module project and any path under the multi-module reactor (the reactor root or any file nested inside any of its modules) always yields two distinct workspace ids -- the two roots never resolve to the same id.
rationale: Whether two paths share a root is itself a decision outcome driven by which pom.xml/reactor a path's ancestors resolve to, so a decision table pairing single-module-root rows against multi-module-root rows and asserting inequality is the direct technique [INV-ROUTE-3]; it falsifies an implementation deriving the id from something coarser than the resolved root -- e.g. a shared cache-root hash or a first-resolved/default workspace -- that would make two distinct project roots collide.
